stances.claim: The Senate should use North Cotabato v. Government (especially SAJ Carpio's separate opinion listing 36 unconstitutional MOA-AD provisions and CJ Sereno's 72-page memorandum) as its essential guide to craft a constitutionally sound BBL.

The BBL cannot cede territory, impair three-branch prerogatives, or override the president's control over executive offices -- but the president has only general supervision (not control) over local governments.
Regional offices of independent commissions may be established but cannot replace or lessen the national offices' constitutional authority.
stances.rhetorical_move: limiting principle on devolution of constitutional bodies

stances.claim: The Bangsamoro police must remain part of and answerable to the PNP because the Constitution mandates a nationally-scoped police force.
stances.rhetorical_move: constitutional textual argument against a separate Bangsamoro police

stances.claim: A parliamentary Bangsamoro structure with a chief minister elected by Bangsamoro MPs is not unconstitutional -- what the Constitution does not prohibit is allowed.
Laws are presumed constitutional and the BBL is too vital to be invalidated in its entirety -- only clearly unconstitutional parts should be set aside.
The key to Mindanao peace is a delicate balancing of constitutional parameters with the justness and legitimacy of the Bangsamoro people's aspirations.

notable_anecdotes: Author substituting written columns for his in-person Senate appearances -- a gesture of institutional respect for the Senate's need for his views, even in his absence.
SAJ Carpio's separate opinion in North Cotabato listing 36 specific unconstitutional provisions of the MOA-AD -- a still-actionable legislative checklist for the Senate.
CJ Sereno's 72-page memorandum in North Cotabato as counsel for petitioner Sen. Drilon -- a document the Senate was advised to study for BBL crafting.

The control-vs-supervision distinction: the President controls executive offices (review/reverse/modify acts) but merely supervises LGUs/autonomous regions (ensure faithful execution) -- a constitutional line the BBL must not cross.

one_paragraph_summary: Having been invited by the Senate twice to speak on Cha-cha and twice on the BBL -- all four times absent due to prior commitments -- Panganiban substitutes written analysis for the BBL hearing. He advises the Senate BBL subcommittee (chaired by Sen. Juan Miguel Zubiri) to use North Cotabato v. Government (October 14, 2008, per J. Conchita Carpio Morales) as its essential constitutional guide -- particularly SAJ Carpio's separate opinion listing 36 unconstitutional provisions of the MOA-AD, and CJ Sereno's 72-page memorandum as counsel for petitioner Sen. Drilon. He notes that Philconsa v. Government (November 29, 2016) held that a pre-enactment challenge to the CAB and FAB was premature. He lays out the constitutional parameters: autonomous regions must fall within PH sovereignty and territorial integrity; the BBL cannot cede territory or impair three-branch prerogatives; executive offices are subject to the president's control while autonomous regions are subject only to general supervision (not control); regional offices of independent commissions may be established but cannot replace national offices; the Bangsamoro police must remain part of the PNP (constitutionally national in scope); and a parliamentary Bangsamoro structure with a chief minister elected by MPs is permissible because what the Constitution does not prohibit is allowed. He closes with the presumption of constitutionality -- the BBL is too vital to be invalidated in its entirety -- and the synthesizing principle: a delicate balancing of constitutional parameters with the justness and legitimacy of the Bangsamoro people's aspirations is the key to peace.
